summary: vanexa-agent daemon executes remote commands from third-party Cloudflare Worker relay
details: The package ships a daemon (started via the `vanexa-agent` bin) that connects to a hardcoded Cloudflare Worker at `vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev` and pipes network-sourced messages into child_process / powershell.exe sinks on the installer's host, giving the relay operator remote code-execution reach into any machine running the daemon. The relay subdomain is on the `hanazaki542` Cloudflare account, which differs from the npm publisher scope `@ikbal_fadilah_vanexa01`, so the party controlling the C2 plane is not the same identity as the package publisher. A second hardcoded endpoint, `vanexa-ai-proxy.hanazaki542.workers.dev`, is listed alongside first-party LLM endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen dashscope) and routes the user's prompts and provider API keys through the same third-party account, contradicting the README's 'no middleman / bring your own key' claim. A third URL, `https://vanexa-agent-fallback.yourdomain.com/agent`, is an unfilled template placeholder. The daemon fires only when the operator explicitly runs `vanexa-agent start`, not on `npm install` or `require()`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
